Publishers assembling books, newsletters and websites strip diacritics from headings, pull quotes and navigation labels where oversized or repeated marks would look cluttered at large sizes.

Repeated diacritics in a single word are all handled in one pass, so heavily vocalized text becomes clean in a single operation.

sections.heading: When Tashkeel Is Worth Keeping
paragraphs: For all the convenience of stripped text, some contexts genuinely benefit from diacritics. Beginning readers, children's books and formal religious texts often depend on vowel marks to disambiguate pronunciation and grammatical function.

If your audience relies on vocalization to read correctly, stripping it could reduce comprehension rather than improve it. The tool is one option in a balanced toolkit, and you should decide per project whether marks help or hinder.
For archival and long-term storage, keeping the fully vocalized version is often wise while the clean version serves display and interchange needs.
The right choice depends on your audience and purpose, not on the availability of the tool.
